title: Introduce declarative unit-econ presets and telemetry adaptor
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: customers regularly ask for sensible defaults for batching, caching and quantization that map to clear unit-economic outcomes. We need a declarative way to encode tenant-level presets, a small telemetry adaptor to assign and evaluate those presets against live metrics, and tooling to safely preview and backfill assignments. This PR introduces: 1) a declarative presets format (YAML) and a lightweight parser in the control plane that exposes a /admin/unit-econ-presets endpoint; 2) a telemetry adaptor that consumes existing infra metrics and emits econ.assigned_profile, econ.estimated_savings, econ.confidence as meter-level metrics; 3) a dry-run CLI (redwood econ preview) that simulates applying presets to a tenant and produces an estimate report; 4) a backfill migration that assigns a best-effort preset to tenants missing explicit profiles (guarded behind a feature flag); 5) automated unit tests and integration smoke tests for the adaptor and CLI; 6) documentation and example presets in examples/unit-econ-presets/*. Why this shape: declarative YAML is easy for SRE/product to author and audit, the adaptor decouples ML inference of best-fit profile from enforcement, and the dry-run/backfill tooling reduces risk for gradual rollouts. Changes: - control plane: api/admin/unit_econ_presets.go (implements CRUD + validation + syntax errors with line numbers) - telemetry: services/telemetry/econ_adaptor.go (maps metrics, computes confidence, emits counters and histograms) - cli: tools/redwood-econ/cmd_preview.go (dry-run mode, CSV/JSON report) - migration: db/migrations/20260218_backfill_unit_econ.sql + migration runner changes with feature flag gating - examples and docs: docs/ops/econ-presets.md and examples/unit-econ-presets/* - tests: telemetry/*_test.go and cli/*_test.go Rollout plan: 1) merge behind feature flag; 2) enable adaptor in staging for 48h to validate metrics distribution and verify econ.estimated_savings is reasonable; 3) run redwood econ preview for top 10 tenants and manually inspect; 4) enable backfill for a small subset (10 tenants) with audit logging; 5) slowly expand. Backwards compatibility: control plane accepts both the new YAML presets and legacy JSON defaults; when both present explicit tenant config wins. Security/audit: CRUD requires platform-admin role, all changes recorded in audit log with diffs. Migration risks: backfill is best-effort and reversible — it writes assignments to a new table unit_econ_assignments with tenant_id and profile_id and a ttl column so it can be rolled back by deleting rows. Testing notes: - unit tests for parsing include malformed YAML cases and overlap/conflict semantics - integration test spins up telemetry mock and verifies econ.* metrics emitted - CLI dry-run compares estimated tokens and costs against a synthetic workload. Checklist: [x] API & validation [x] Telemetry adaptor [x] CLI dry-run [x] Backfill migration (feature flagged) [x] Unit + integration tests [x] Docs and examples [ ] Add end-to-end benchmark comparing inference costs (follow-up ticket).

release_notes: Add declarative unit-economic presets, a telemetry adaptor that emits econ.* metrics, a CLI dry-run preview, and a feature-flagged backfill migration. Operators can author YAML presets and preview estimated savings before applying. Migration is reversible and opt-out aware.
